issue.title: Unattributed GH013 secret rejections re-push the same agents batch every drain instead of isolating clean units

task_type_fields.impact:
The sase-1oh.5.1 plan (phase rejection-recovery, step 1) asked for this: "If locations are absent or ambiguous, reset the rejected batch and replay independently valid units with bounded attempts to isolate failures; never blame an arbitrary clean row or retire the whole project indefinitely."

Current behavior is bounded per drain, sanitized, and blames nothing. It does not isolate, though, so clean publication for the project stalls for as long as the unattributed content stays in the batch.

Practical likelihood is low: GitHub push-protection GH013 output normally carries `locations: commit/path`, and the core classifier attributes those. Expect this only for an unfamiliar output format or truncated location lists. Before this epic, any GH013 stalled all publication, so this is a residual gap, not a regression.

Suggested direction: after an unattributed secret rejection and reset, replay independently valid units (for example one hood per commit and push) with a bounded number of attempts per drain. Park only the unit whose isolated push is still rejected, using sanitized, uncharged or quarantining per-request accounting. Every other unit keeps publishing.
task_type_fields.repro:
1. In `tests/agents_sync/test_publication_recovery.py`, `test_no_location_rejection_resets_without_blaming_a_clean_row` sends a GH013 stderr with no `path:` locations. `recover_publication_push` returns `rebuild_clean` with `blocked_paths == ()`.
2. Follow both callers: `git_sync_transaction._retry_after_secret_recovery` and the commit-drain retry in `commit_publication_transaction.py` (around the second `recover_publication_push` call). Each rebuilds the same batch, pushes once more, receives the same unattributed rejection, and stops with the sanitized "no path could be attributed" error.
3. The next drain prepares the same batch again, so every drain makes two rejected pushes. No clean unit from that project reaches the remote until the offending content leaves the batch some other way.

issue.creation_reason: The sase-1oh.5.1 lander found that the rejection-recovery phase (sase-1oh.5.1.4) resets and replays the whole batch when a secret-scan rejection names no path, so clean publication for that project can stall indefinitely. The isolation the plan required was deferred as a distinct follow-up.
